source.version: arXiv 2409.14228 v1 of 2024-09-21 (PDF on file, set in the CHI '25 template with placeholder DOI), not the ACM version of record 10.1145/3706598.3713952
source.title_on_document: Mentigo: An Intelligent Agent for Mentoring Students in the Creative Problem Solving Process

supplement.where: The paper refers to 'supplementary materials' (p. 11, Section 5.3.2; p. 12, Section 5.3.4) and gives no URL.
supplement.holds: Details of the four-dimension evaluation matrix for the learning reports and the interview protocol outline.

paper_design_summary: Twelve middle-school students (ages 12 to 14) each did two creative problem-solving tasks (Smart Home, Low-Carbon Campus) in a within-subject design: one with Mentigo, a GPT-4o mentor agent that asks guiding questions and adapts strategies to the student's state, and one with a baseline version of the agent with simple prompts. Condition order was counterbalanced and randomized. Three researchers rated each learning report on quality, elaboration, originality, and human-like expression, and the authors also compared questionnaires and coded student dialogue.

studies.label: Within-subject user study: Mentigo vs. baseline agent on two CPS tasks

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two conditions (Mentigo agent vs. baseline agent) and the pairing of conditions with the two CPS tasks; every student used both systems.
assignment.quote: Participants were asked to complete CPS tasks under two conditions in a counterbalanced and randomized order: the system condition (using our fully designed educational agent with advanced features) and the baseline condition
assignment.locator: p. 10, Section 5.2; also p. 10, Section 5.1 ('We employed a randomized within-subject experimental design') and p. 10, Section 5.2 phase (3)

arms.name: Mentigo (system condition)
arms.description: Fully designed GPT-4o mentor agent with dynamic prompts, reflective questions, adaptive feedback, and a six-stage CPS workflow; 30 minutes on the task, then a learning report.

arms.name: Baseline condition
arms.description: Basic version of the agent with simple prompts and a consistent interface, lacking Mentigo's advanced features; 30 minutes on the other task, then a learning report.

participants.exclusions: The paper gives no n for any analysis. It says two students did not complete the last two stages with Mentigo and their incomplete data were excluded from the final analysis (p. 14, Section 6.3), which suggests 10 students in at least the engagement analysis. The count analyzed is at most 12 in every analysis. Each student appears in both arms.
participants.who: Middle-school students aged 12 to 14 (6 boys, 6 girls; grades 7 to 9), recruited through social media; sessions run remotely over Tencent Meeting with a researcher present.
participants.quote: We recruited 12 middle school students aged 12 to 14 (6 males and 6 females) for this study (shown in Table 4).
participants.locator: p. 10, Section 5.1; p. 11, Table 4 (P1 to P12)

ai_tool.name_model: Mentigo, built on OpenAI GPT-4o API (version 2024-08-06) with Langchain; the baseline is a basic version of the same agent with simple prompts
ai_tool.how_used: Mentigo provides adaptive mentoring through six CPS stages, selecting guiding questions, strategies, feedback, encouragement, and example problem statements according to the student's state. Its examples supply task content (p. 16, Figure 5, left panel); participants also describe receiving ideas from Mentigo (p. 13, Section 6.2). The baseline answers requests and, per the experts, often generated multiple answers for the student to pick from (p. 15, Section 6.4).

task.description: Creative problem solving: identify problems and propose solutions for smart home systems (one task) or low-carbon practices on a school campus (other task), ending in a written learning report with the proposed solutions and rationale.
task.duration: 30 minutes per task (section heading says 30 to 40 minutes each)

outcomes.name: Learning-report score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three researchers independently rated each learning report using an evaluation matrix adapted from Urban et al. (2024) with four dimensions: Quality, Elaboration, Originality, and Human-like Expression (p. 11, Section 5.3.2). The paper reports one learning-report score comparison (p. 13, Section 6.2), but does not identify the score as a total/composite or explain aggregation across dimensions or raters. The aggregation rule and score scale cannot be confirmed from this PDF; evaluation-matrix details are referred to supplementary materials absent from this PDF. The ratings were performed by researchers.

contrasts.reported: Mentigo M = 13.43, SD = 3.17 vs baseline M = 10.74, SD = 2.72; independent samples t-test, p = 0.016 (n per arm not printed)

outcomes.name: Creation-level utterances in student dialogue
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Students' speech to the agent hand-coded by Bloom's taxonomy level; 'Creation' = creating new ideas using what has just been learned (Table 5). Analysis, Evaluation, and other levels are reported in the same table.

contrasts.reported: Creation: Mentigo Mdn = 7.5 vs baseline Mdn = 2; U = 81.5, p = 0.0180*

outcomes.name: CPS knowledge post-test
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Post-test questionnaire on CPS knowledge; the paper says knowledge gain reflects 'changes in participants' self-rated knowledge on CPS tasks' (p. 11, Section 5.3.1). Not scored on the creative output.

contrasts.reported: Post-test Mentigo 6.67 (2.19) vs baseline 5 (1.91); effect size 0.77*; p = 0.019* (Mann-Whitney U); text gives Cohen's d = 0.765

eligibility.reason: Randomized, counterbalanced within-subject comparison of two AI configurations (Mentigo vs. a basic agent) on CPS tasks, with researcher ratings of the learning reports. Only 12 students took part (p. 10, Section 5.1; p. 11, Table 4), at most 12 analyzed, far below 50. Listed in the screening report as a small randomized experiment and left out of the dataset.

one_line_finding: In a randomized within-subject study of 12 middle-school students, learning reports written with Mentigo scored higher than those written with a baseline agent (M = 13.43, SD = 3.17 vs. M = 10.74, SD = 2.72; p = 0.016; p. 13, Section 6.2).
